name: WeWork TK Ikedayama
card: Three minutes from Gotanda Station, themed on Showa-era nostalgia
title: WeWork TK Ikedayama — interiors evoking Showa-era nostalgia, 3 minutes from Gotanda Station
lead: WeWork TK Ikedayama is on the 2nd floor of the TK Ikedayama Building, a three-minute walk from Gotanda Station, served by three lines. Its interior is built around Showa-era nostalgia, portraying a neighbourhood that is becoming more international while keeping its familiar old scenery. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Completed January 2005 / 19 floors above ground, 1 below
Ceiling height 2,700 mm / 8 meeting rooms / phone booths, parents' room, honesty market and more
concept: Showa-era nostalgia
The interior concept is “Showa nostalgia” — expressing Gotanda, a district growing more international while keeping the familiar scenes of the past, the website says.
Gotanda is home to many leading venture and startup companies, and the website describes new business opportunities arising from exchanges across industries and companies.
steps: A space with a nostalgic feel
The shared areas have interiors that recall the Showa era.
There are eight meeting rooms, plus phone booths, a parents' room and an honesty market.
In a district full of exchange, it is a convenient base for meetings.

word.title: What is the Showa era?
body: Japan's imperial era from 1926 to 1989, often remembered with nostalgia for the post-war decades of growth and their street scenes.
WeWork TK Ikedayama takes “Showa nostalgia” as its interior concept, reflecting Gotanda's lingering old-time scenery.

name: WeWork Hareza Ikebukuro
card: High floors of Ikebukuro's new landmark, inspired by art, Japanese painting and film
title: WeWork Hareza Ikebukuro — interiors inspired by Ikebukuro's art and film, on the upper floors of Hareza Tower
lead: WeWork Hareza Ikebukuro is on the upper floors of Hareza Tower, Ikebukuro's new landmark. One of the largest sites in Japan, it features interiors inspired by the art, Japanese painting and film rooted in Ikebukuro. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Completed May 2020 / 33 floors above ground, 2 below
Ceiling height 2,900 mm / 22 meeting rooms / phone booths, parents' room, honesty market and more
hero_cap: The shared area at WeWork Hareza Ikebukuro
concept: Where business and culture intersect
The website presents Ikebukuro as a district “where business and culture intersect”. The interiors draw on the art, Japanese painting and film rooted in Ikebukuro.
Members range from startups to long-established manufacturers, and the website says new collaborations come out of their exchanges.
steps: Inspired by art and Japanese painting
The shared areas are full of interiors inspired by Ikebukuro's art, Japanese painting and film.
There are 22 meeting rooms, plus phone booths, a parents' room and an honesty market.
Vibration control and triple power feeds
The building uses new-generation vibration-control oil dampers and a spot-network system that receives power on three lines simultaneously, as a safeguard against outages.
Each floor's elevator hall has security gates, and a disaster-prevention centre is staffed 24 hours.

word.title: What is an honesty market?
body: A shop with no staff, where you pay for what you take yourself — “honesty” being the key.
The WeWork website lists it among the facilities at its sites.

name: WeWork Ark Hills South
card: Directly connected to Roppongi-itchome Station — American style with a touch of glamour
title: WeWork Ark Hills South — American style meets glamour, directly connected to Roppongi-itchome Station
lead: WeWork Ark Hills South is on the 16th floor of Ark Hills South Tower, directly connected to Roppongi-itchome Station on the subway. The website highlights its international setting and a design that blends an American feel with glamour. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Completed August 2013 / 20 floors above ground, 3 below
Ceiling height 2,850 mm / 12 meeting rooms / phone booths, parents' room, honesty market and more
concept: American style and glamour
Its design blends an American atmosphere with glamour. In this cosmopolitan area, many companies, global firms among them, use the site, the website says.
The surroundings have green plazas, tree-lined paths and street trees, so you can feel Japan's four seasons in the middle of the city.
steps: A glamorous space leads from the front desk into the shared areas.
There are 12 meeting rooms, plus phone booths, a parents' room and an honesty market.
The building has a vibration-control structure and can supply power to common areas for up to 72 hours in an emergency.

word.title: What is a vibration-control structure?
body: A structure with dampers and other devices built into the building to absorb and reduce earthquake shaking.
Ark Hills South Tower has one, plus backup power for common areas for up to 72 hours in an emergency.

credits: WeWork official website: “WeWork Ark Hills South”

name: The Executive Centre JP Tower
card: Floors 11 and 14 of JP Tower, the former Tokyo Central Post Office, with a barista bar overlooking the station
title: The Executive Centre JP Tower — serviced offices and coworking on the 11th and 14th floors, directly connected to Tokyo Station
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 11th and 14th floors of JP Tower, directly connected to Tokyo Station. JP Tower is the former Tokyo Central Post Office, reborn as an office building in 2013. It has a bar with a resident barista, a members' lounge and five meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The former Tokyo Central Post Office, reborn as offices in 2013; directly connected to Tokyo Station
Private offices / coworking (hot desks, dedicated desks) / 5 meeting rooms / event space
concept: A workplace overlooking Tokyo Station
The website lists the centre's features as “unrivalled views of Tokyo Station”, “direct connection to Tokyo Station” and “abundant natural light”.
Art Deco design, a large refreshment area and switchable “magic glass” windows for privacy are also features. An international serviced office now operates inside a building with a postal history.
steps: Rooms for teams and five meeting rooms
Private offices come with height-adjustable desks, and there are five meeting rooms.
Outside the windows are Tokyo Station's red-brick building and the streets of Marunouchi.

word.title: What is magic glass?
body: Glass that switches electrically between clear and frosted. The website highlights magic-glass windows for privacy.
One pane gives you both openness and screening during meetings.

credits: The Executive Centre official website: “JP Tower”

name: The Executive Centre Shin-Marunouchi Center
card: White marble, oak and leather on floors 20–21
title: The Executive Centre Shin-Marunouchi Center Building — a wood-textured workplace on floors 20–21, connected underground to Tokyo Station
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 20th and 21st floors of the Shin-Marunouchi Center Building, connected underground to Tokyo Station. The website describes interiors with softly lit wood textures and finishes of white marble, oak and fine leather. There are six meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre Shin-Marunouchi Center Building
Connected underground to Tokyo Station; Gold green-building certification (per the official site)
Private offices / coworking (hot desks, dedicated desks) / 6 meeting rooms
concept: Two floors of wood and marble
The website describes the interior as “softly lit wood textures” with refined finishes of white marble, oak and fine leather.
Spanning the 20th and 21st floors, it leads from a striking reception to a refreshment area, private offices and meeting rooms.
steps: The reception, singled out by the website for its presence, is where visitors are welcomed.
Beside it is a lounge where visitors wait.
Places to relax and to work
There is a refreshment area for breaks and chats, and coworking seats.
Hot desks and dedicated desks start at ¥54,000 a month; day passes from ¥5,000 a day.
Rooms for teams and six meeting rooms
Private offices are priced on request, and there are six meeting rooms.
One meeting room holds 16, suitable for larger meetings.

word.title: What is green building certification?
body: Certification that rates a building's environmental performance and consideration for its users. According to the website, the Shin-Marunouchi Center Building has Gold certification.
For tenants, it is one useful yardstick when choosing a building.

name: The Executive Centre Roppongi Hills North Tower
card: Light oak and shoji-style meeting rooms on floors 16–17
title: The Executive Centre Roppongi Hills North Tower — floors 16–17 with shoji-style meeting rooms, directly connected to Roppongi Station
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 16th and 17th floors of Roppongi Hills North Tower, directly connected to Roppongi Station. The website describes light oak finishes inspired by nature and meeting rooms like shoji screens. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre Roppongi Hills North Tower
Light oak finishes, shoji-style meeting rooms (per the official site)
Private offices / coworking (hot desks, dedicated desks) / 3 meeting rooms
concept: An interior inspired by nature
According to the website, the design takes its inspiration from nature, using delicate light-oak surfaces.
The meeting rooms recall Japanese shoji screens. It sits inside Roppongi Hills, surrounded by restaurants, hotels and homes.
steps: A corridor runs from reception to a waiting area.
The centre spans two floors, the 16th and 17th.
The refreshment area and coworking seats are open to members.
Hot desks and dedicated desks start at ¥54,000 a month; day passes from ¥5,000 a day.
Shoji-style meeting rooms and city views
Private offices are priced on request and have height-adjustable desks. There are three meeting rooms, and the website highlights their city views.

word.title: What is shoji?
body: A traditional Japanese sliding screen of washi paper on a wooden lattice. It lets soft light through while blocking sightlines.
The website describes the centre's meeting rooms as shoji-style — bringing Japanese light into a glass high-rise.

credits: © The Executive Centre (official website “Roppongi Hills North Tower”)

name: The Executive Centre Sanno Park Tower
card: A quiet 3rd-floor workplace near the National Diet Building
title: The Executive Centre Sanno Park Tower — a quiet 3rd floor directly connected to Tameike-Sanno and Kokkai-gijido-mae stations
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 3rd floor of Sanno Park Tower, directly connected to Tameike-Sanno and Kokkai-gijido-mae stations, close to the National Diet Building and the Prime Minister's Office. The website describes a refined, minimal fit-out and a quiet, calm environment. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre Sanno Park Tower
Directly connected to Tameike-Sanno and Kokkai-gijido-mae stations (per the official site)
Private offices / coworking (hot desks, dedicated desks) / 3 meeting rooms / event space
concept: A quiet workplace in the political district
The website describes the centre as being at the political heart of Chiyoda-ku, near the National Diet Building and the Prime Minister's Office.
The interior is “elegant minimalism”, with meeting rooms in various formats and a quiet environment set apart from its surroundings.
steps: Shared seats and rooms for teams
There are coworking seats and private offices priced on request.
Hot desks and dedicated desks start at ¥54,000 a month; day passes from ¥5,000 a day.
There are three meeting rooms in different formats, plus a function room usable as an event space.
Outside the windows are the streets of Akasaka and Nagatacho.

word.title: What is a function room?
body: A multipurpose room for briefings, small events and more.
The centre at Sanno Park Tower has a function room usable as an event space.

credits: © The Executive Centre (official website “Sanno Park Tower”)

name: The Executive Centre Cerulean Tower
card: A tea-room-inspired reception and a 15th floor with views of Mt Fuji
title: The Executive Centre Cerulean Tower — a tea-room-inspired reception and views of Mt Fuji, on the 15th floor in Shibuya
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 15th floor of Cerulean Tower, a five-minute walk from Shibuya Station. Completed in 2001, Cerulean Tower was the tallest building around Shibuya Station until 2019. The website describes a reception inspired by the Japanese tea room, and views over Tokyo to Mt Fuji. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Completed 2001; a high-rise of offices and a hotel (per the official site)
Private offices / coworking (hot desks, dedicated desks) / 2 meeting rooms / virtual office
concept: A reception inspired by the tea room
The website's signature feature is a reception inspired by the Japanese tea room: on the 15th floor of a Shibuya skyscraper, visitors are first greeted by a Japanese setting.
Spacious coworking and collaboration areas and views of Tokyo and Mt Fuji are also listed among the centre's features.
steps: Coworking seats the website calls “spacious”, and a pantry with drinks.
Hot desks and dedicated desks start at ¥54,000 a month, day passes from ¥5,000 a day and virtual offices from ¥16,200 a month.
Private offices are priced on request, and there are two meeting rooms.
The windows look out over Shibuya, and on clear days Mt Fuji is visible, the website says.

word.title: What is a Japanese tea room?
body: A small room designed for the tea ceremony — a space shaped by simple materials and the etiquette of welcoming guests.
The centre at Cerulean Tower has a reception inspired by it.

credits: The Executive Centre official website: “Cerulean Tower”

name: The Executive Centre Jingumae Tower
card: British and Japanese interiors on floors 12–14, overlooking Yoyogi Park
title: The Executive Centre Jingumae Tower Building — British-meets-Japanese interiors on floors 12–14 in Harajuku
lead: The Executive Centre has a centre on the 12th to 14th floors of the Jingumae Tower Building, on the corner of Takeshita-dori in Harajuku. The website describes “an interior where Britain meets Japan”: polished oak floors, navy patterned wallpaper and vintage furniture. There are nine meeting rooms. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: The Executive Centre Jingumae Tower Building
Polished oak floors, navy patterned wallpaper, vintage furniture by Timothy Oulton (per the official site)
Private offices / coworking (hot desks, dedicated desks) / 9 meeting rooms / library
concept: Where Britain meets Japan
According to the website, the centre adds artistic details reflecting trendy Harajuku to The Executive Centre's signature design.
Traditional polished oak floors are paired with navy patterned wallpaper and vintage furniture by Timothy Oulton. From its three floors, Yoyogi Park and Mt Fuji are visible, the website says.
steps: Reception leads into the coworking lounge.
The lounge has the vintage furniture the website describes.
Hot desks and rooms for teams
Hot-desk seating and private offices priced on request. Private offices have height-adjustable desks and Herman Miller chairs.
Hot desks and dedicated desks start at ¥54,000 a month; day passes from ¥5,000 a day.
There are nine meeting rooms, presented by the website as well suited to meetings and discussions.
The windows look out over both city and greenery.

word.title: What is vintage furniture?
body: Furniture with the character that comes with age — a worn-in texture new pieces don't have.
The website says the Jingumae Tower Building centre is furnished with vintage pieces by Timothy Oulton.
